extracted.intended_audience: SF/F short fiction writers, Clarion-style workshop participants and instructors
extracted.subtask_description: A rubric and workshop method for peer critique of science fiction and fantasy short fiction (Clarion/Milford tradition): daily group critiques with author silence followed by reply, using implicit craft dimensions to evaluate stories. Also includes recent reforms toward author-centered and culturally aware critique.

rubrics_metrics.name: Concept / Idea (Idea freshness)
rubrics_metrics.description: Is the central science-fictional or fantasy idea fresh? Is it productively complicated, or merely thrown in? Has it been done before, and if so, what is added?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate originality and productive use of speculative element: a strong idea should feel fresh and integrated, not tacked on. Consider whether the idea is developed in ways that add something beyond prior treatments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Worldbuilding (Internal consistency)
rubrics_metrics.description: Is the imagined world internally consistent? Are the rules clear (or productively ambiguous)? Does the world's strangeness emerge through detail, not exposition?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Favor showing world details through story action and texture rather than exposition. Anti-pattern: 'Lore-dumping' — long chunks of backstory, worldbuilding, or technical explanation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plot (Shape and earned ending)
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the story have a shape? Is the conflict productive? Does the protagonist drive events or merely observe? Is the ending earned?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess narrative arc, conflict dynamics, protagonist agency, and whether the climax follows logically from what came before. Watch for deus ex machina or abrupt, unsupported resolutions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Character (Distinctness and agency)
rubrics_metrics.description: Are characters distinct in voice, body, motivation? Are protagonists active? Do secondary characters serve the story without being flat? Does the protagonist change?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look for distinct voices and embodied description, clear motivations, and arcs (change/agency). Anti-patterns include passive protagonists and flat secondary characters who exist only to deliver info or move the plot.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prose (Sentence-level competence and voice)
rubrics_metrics.description: Sentence-level competence; voice consistency; POV discipline (no head-hopping); show vs. tell judgment; cliché elimination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Critique should address grammar, clarity, stylistic voice, maintenance of a consistent point of view, appropriate use of showing rather than telling, and removal of clichés. These are micro-level craft standards foundational for stronger work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pacing
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the story hold attention? Are there sagging middles? Is the climax timed appropriately?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate rhythm and momentum across the story; note sections that drag or rush, and whether the story builds toward and times its climax effectively.

rubrics_metrics.name: Genre Engagement
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the story know its genre conventions? Does it deploy or knowingly violate them? Is it accessible to genre readers without being pandering?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess awareness and handling of SF/F tropes: effective stories either work within conventions skillfully or subvert them with purpose, avoiding pandering to genre expectations while remaining intelligible to genre audiences.

rubrics_metrics.name: The infodump (Anti-pattern)
rubrics_metrics.description: Backstory, worldbuilding, or tech explained in chunks ('lore-dumping' is the universal critique).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Flag large blocks of exposition that halt narrative momentum. Recommend integrating necessary information through scenes, dialogue, and detail rather than expository lumps.

rubrics_metrics.name: The passive protagonist (Anti-pattern)
rubrics_metrics.description: Events happen TO the character rather than from their choices — the protagonist is passive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourage rewriting to give protagonists agency: make them make decisions that drive plot rather than just react, and ensure their motivations compel their actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: The unearned ending (Anti-pattern)
rubrics_metrics.description: Climax not set up by what came before; deus ex machina; endings like 'and then they woke up.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Require that resolutions be foreshadowed and grounded in established stakes and character decisions; call out sudden or convenient fixes that undercut narrative credibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Workshop method: daily critique with author silence (Milford Method)
rubrics_metrics.description: Daily critique sessions covering all student stories; author silence during critique (Milford Method) followed by reply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This procedural rule structures how feedback is given: the author listens without interrupting, then responds. It shapes the tone and content of comments and emphasizes peer observations before author defense.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid privileging Western/Anglophone craft norms
rubrics_metrics.description: Traditional workshop can privilege Western/Anglophone craft norms and be hostile to writers from underrepresented communities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Critiquers should be aware of cultural framing and avoid judging work solely by Western genre or stylistic norms. Consider cultural context and values when evaluating choices that may reflect different traditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Author-centered critique and cultural-context consideration (Reforms)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reforms include author-centered dialogue (not pure silence); cultural-context briefings; critique of work on its own terms, not against external genre norms; time for the writer to set their own evaluation criteria.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When conducting critique, allow space for the author to set evaluation priorities and provide cultural/contextual information. Shift from ritualized critique-confidence toward dialog that respects the writer's aims and background.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarion implicit summary rubric (Nine checklist items)
rubrics_metrics.description: Implicit rubric summarized as: 1) Idea freshness; 2) World internal consistency; 3) Plot shape and earned ending; 4) Character distinctness and agency; 5) Sentence-level prose; 6) Voice and POV discipline; 7) Pacing; 8) Genre engagement; 9) Absence of infodumps, passivity, unearned endings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this compact checklist as an integrated evaluation: passing most or all items makes a story 'workshop-strong'; failing several leads to harsher critique. This consolidates the workshop's recurring focus areas.
